headline: Two BLOCKER regressions found in the D1 change I authored. Both CONFIRMED real. They would have broken code indexing silently.

findings.evidence: indexing_pipeline.py: content_response is bound ONLY in the contextualized else-branch (:322) but read unconditionally at the embedding-cost sum (:344 pre-fix). With D1 the flat branch is the default, so every code file raises UnboundLocalError. Reproduced: driving _process_file against the repo source yields 'cannot access local variable content_response where it is not associated with a value'.
findings.severity_is_worse_than_a_crash: _process_file wraps the body in except Exception: log, progress.errors += 1, return ([], []). The error is therefore SWALLOWED — code indexing silently produces zero documents and reports an error count, rather than failing loudly.

findings.evidence: standard_embedder.embed_batch returns List[EmbeddingResponse] (voyage_embedder.py:336). The flat branch assigned that list straight to content_embeddings, and the document builder does content_vector = content_embeddings[i] with a now-false comment '# Already List[float]'. title/breadcrumb correctly unwrap via .embedding; content did not. Qdrant would receive an object instead of a float list.

Auditor ruled that leaving truncation: bool = True as VoyageEmbedder's default is NOT defensible because it traps the next caller. That is a fair criticism of my scope reasoning. The file is outside the ADR-226 carve-out, so flipping the default requires its own amendment and a review of every existing caller — it cannot ride on this packet. Recorded as required follow-up, NOT closed.

Correct that the AST tests hardcode two files, so a flat embed added elsewhere escapes them. Mitigated this round by the new behavioural test that drives _process_file and asserts on truncation kwargs actually passed at runtime, which is file-location independent for that path. A full-tree AST sweep remains a reasonable follow-up.

Auditor: retaining the original substring test alongside the AST tests is misleading and masks their narrow scope. Agreed — I kept it for 'extra coverage' and that was wrong reasoning; a test that cannot fail meaningfully is negative value. Should be removed.

f001_regression_check: PASS — auditor re-verified at this head; carve-out anchoring, traversal refusal, and the _FALLBACK_FORBIDDEN subset invariant all intact.
why_five_rounds_missed_this: Every prior round reasoned about the diff or read source statically. No test drove IndexingPipeline._process_file, so a green 123-test suite coexisted with a totally broken flat indexing path. The gap I had already flagged as NOT_RUN — 'live index->search roundtrip' — is exactly where both BLOCKERs lived. Static review is not a substitute for executing the path.
